findings.title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
findings.body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only fires the optional `onSuccess`/`onChanged` callback on success; it never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (unlike `disconnectMutation`, which explicitly invalidates it in `onSettled`). The `cacheUpdatedAt` shown in this component comes from that internal `connectedCalendars` query in `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper`. Unless the consumer's `onChanged` happens to refetch that exact query (it is not guaranteed to), the dropdown keeps showing the stale "Cache Status / Last updated" entry and the "Delete cached data" action after the cache has already been deleted, so the UI misreports that cached data still exists until a manual page refresh.

findings.title: Overwriting SelectedCalendar.updatedAt on cache repopulation conflates cache refresh with calendar change
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` ends with `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`, whose comment says it updates `updatedAt` for all calendars of the credential. `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is also written by the Google webhook handler to record when a calendar's contents actually changed. Bumping it whenever the cache is (re)populated therefore overwrites that "last calendar change" signal with "last cache write", which can corrupt any consumer relying on `updatedAt` to detect real changes. Additionally, passing an empty `data: {}` to Prisma `updateMany` to trigger the `@updatedAt` side effect is fragile — if Prisma performs no update for empty data the intended timestamp bump silently never happens. This write is redundant given the UI reads `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCache` instead.

findings.title: Cache status query ignores expiresAt, reporting timestamps for expired caches
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows for the given credentials and returns `max(updatedAt)` without filtering on `expiresAt >= now()`. When every cached entry for a credential has expired (i.e. no cache is actually servable), the handler still returns an `updatedAt`, and the UI renders a "Cache Status — Last updated" entry plus the "Delete cached data" action for a cache that contains no usable data. This misleads the user into thinking availability is currently being served from cache. The `where` clause should exclude expired rows (or the UI should distinguish expired vs. live cache).

findings.title: Cache timestamp formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
findings.body: The "Last updated" timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` regardless of the user's locale, so non-English users see US date/time formatting even though the surrounding strings are localized via `t()`. This should derive the locale from `useLocale()` (or the user's time zone/locale) so the date matches the rest of the localized UI.

findings.title: sed -i '' syntax fails on GNU/Linux
findings.body: The script uses `sed -i '' -E "s|...|...|"` to rewrite `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` in the env file. The empty-string argument to `-i` is BSD/macOS sed syntax; on GNU sed (the common Linux dev/CI environment) it is interpreted as the script name and errors out, so the env file is never updated and the webhook URL is not applied. The script also shells out to `tmole` without checking that it is installed, and derives `ENV_FILE="../.env"` relative to the current working directory rather than the script location.
